## Appearance

Gilbert is a tall, broad-shouldered fellow with a frank face, curly brown hair, hazel eyes, and a teasing smile. At times he has appeared pale and thin, and he later looks very young for a doctor.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050), [v3 ch.Weddings P22](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0022), [v4 CHAPTER 2 THE HOUSE OF DREAMS P14](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0014)_

## Personality

Gilbert is a clever, good-natured, and teasing young fellow who possesses a sense of humor, ambition, and a strong zest for life. Thoughtful and kind, he is determined to put the best into life and get the best out of it. He is a hardworking individual who aims to earn his own way through college, having ultimately made up his mind that he wants to become a doctor.

## History

Gilbert Blythe returned to [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) after spending three years in Alberta with his sick father and a summer visiting cousins. Upon his return to school, he pulled [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) Shirley's braid and called her 'Carrots,' prompting her to smash a slate over his head and refuse his apology. Their fierce academic rivalry continued through their school years, though Gilbert eventually saved [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) from a leaking boat on the pond and offered his friendship, which she angrily rejected. After completing his studies at Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) and winning the medal, Gilbert gave up his appointment at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school so [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) could take it, leading them to finally end their feud and become close friends. Gilbert then attended [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college), where he led his freshman class to victory in the Arts Rush and co-founded the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers) during his breaks. During their time at college, Gilbert confessed his love and proposed to [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), but she rejected him, breaking his heart and severing their close friendship. After recovering from a life-threatening bout of typhoid fever, he proposed to her a second time in [Hester](../character/hester-gray.md) Gray's garden, and she happily accepted. Following their wedding, Gilbert carried [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) into their new house at [Four Winds Harbor](../codex/places.md#four-winds-harbor), where he established his medical practice. When he realized that their neighbor [Dick](../character/dick-moore.md) Moore's memory could be restored through surgery, he dutifully informed [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) despite Anne's objections, a choice that ultimately revealed [Dick](../character/dick-moore.md) was actually his cousin George. Following the loss of their firstborn infant, Joyce, Gilbert and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) welcomed a healthy baby boy named James Matthew. Gilbert eventually proposed buying the [Morgan](../character/morgan.md) place in the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen), leading the couple to move into their new home after saying goodbye to their house of dreams.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Quotes

> "It wasn’t particularly good of me at all, Anne. I was pleased to be able to do you some small service. Are we going to be friends after this? Have you really forgiven me my old fault?"
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P52](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0052)

> "We were born to be good friends, Anne. You’ve thwarted destiny enough. I know we can help each other in many ways. You are going to keep up your studies, aren’t you? So am I. Come, I’m going to walk home with you."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P55](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0055)

> “Not she,” said Gilbert emphatically. “I know Louisa Spencer well. She doesn’t ‘believe’ in Village Improvement Societies, but she does believe in dollars and cents. She’d be more likely to urge Judson on than to dissuade him.”
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P46](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0046)

> "It’s a nice old burg, they tell me, and has the finest natural park in the world. I’ve heard that the scenery in it is magnificent."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v3 ch.Change P22](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0022)

> "You’re just tired, Anne. Come, forget it all and take a walk with me—a ramble back through the woods beyond the marsh. There should be something there I want to show you."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v3 ch.Autumn P15](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0015)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--gilbert-blythe.md)

Gilbert and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) began as bitter enemies in school after Gilbert teased her, prompting [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to smash a slate over his head and hold a persistent grudge despite his attempts to apologize and save her from a leaking boat [R3, R4, S1, S4]. They gradually transitioned into intense academic rivals, literary collaborators, and close friends as [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) eventually forgave him [R1, R5, R6, S5]. Though [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) initially rejected his marriage proposal, their relationship deepened until they ultimately married, settling down together as husband and wife [R2, R7, S41, S67].

### [Cornelia Bryant](../character/cornelia-bryant.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/cornelia-bryant--gilbert-blythe.md)

Miss Cornelia [Bryant](../character/cornelia-bryant.md) is a frequent visitor to Gilbert's home and a friend to his household [R18, S44]. Though she holds outspoken and sharp opinions about men, she enjoys staying for tea and engaging in lively debates that Gilbert secretly finds amusing [S45, S46].

### [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/gilbert-blythe--leslie-moore.md)

Gilbert and [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) are good friends who frequently spend pleasant firelight evenings together discussing books or visiting Captain Jim at the lighthouse [R20, S57, S58]. ### [Uncle Jim](../character/uncle-jim.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/gilbert-blythe--uncle-jim.md)

Gilbert and Captain Jim are close friends who consider each other kindred spirits [R22, S63]. Gilbert regularly spends long autumn evenings at Captain Jim's lighthouse engaging in high converse, listening to his sea stories, and sharing hearty laughs over local news [S65, S66, S67].
